title: How to Export BigQuery Logs
content_md: When security logs sit in BigQuery (from a Cloud Logging sink, a Google Workspace export or your own pipeline), export them with EXPORT DATA. It writes newline-delimited JSON to a Cloud Storage bucket, and you download that. For small results, bq query –format=json prints the rows directly. Either way, filter on the table’s time or partition column first, because BigQuery bills by data scanned. BigQuery is where many Google Cloud teams keep log history long after Cloud Logging’s default retention has passed. Prime Core has more than 24,000 unique detection rules, mapped to 676 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get a slice out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start Permissions. You need to run jobs (BigQuery Job User), read the dataset (BigQuery Data Viewer), and write to the export bucket. Know the tables. A Cloud Logging sink to BigQuery creates tables named after the logs, for example cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity, often partitioned by timestamp. Workspace exports have their own schema. Check the cost first. Add –dry_run to a bq query to see how many bytes it would scan. If the number makes you wince, add a tighter time filter.
